findings.evidence: Matching.lean:272 states `hrank : (P.matchingMatrix M k).rank = Fintype.card (P.totalDegreePiece k)`, used via `Matrix.rank_eq_card_iff_mulVec_injective` (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Rank.lean:42: `B.rank = Fintype.card n ↔ Function.Injective B.mulVec`) — injectivity of `mulVec`, i.e. column independence, not pairwise distinctness.
findings.fix: Replace both occurrences with the correct reading, e.g. "no nonzero combination of the operators of total degree `k` has vanishing matrix element in every amplitude" (equivalently, the columns of the matching matrix are linearly independent).
findings.issue: The gloss "the amplitudes separate the operators of total degree `k`" misdescribes `(matchingMatrix M k).rank = card (totalDegreePiece k)`. Separating operators pairwise (distinct columns) is strictly weaker than linear independence of the columns: columns (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) are pairwise distinct but dependent. Same gloss repeated at line 267 in `IsMatching.eqOn_totalDegreePiece`.

findings.evidence: Matching.lean:203-207 defines and documents `isMatching_effectiveAmplitude`, but it appears nowhere in the module docstring's Main results (lines 59-71), which pair with the "existence is not claimed" note at line 78.
findings.fix: Add `PowerCounting.isMatching_effectiveAmplitude` to "Main results" (or one sentence in the implementation notes) noting that the predicate is inhabited by the amplitudes an assignment generates itself.
findings.issue: The Implementation notes say "Existence of a matching assignment is not claimed in general" and the Main results list omits `isMatching_effectiveAmplitude`, so the module docstring gives a reader no indication that `IsMatching` is ever inhabited — the one fact in the file that rules out vacuity.

summary: Documentation is otherwise accurate and well-scoped, but the informal gloss of the full-column-rank condition ("the amplitudes separate the operators") states something strictly weaker than the condition it claims to explain, in both the module docstring and the main uniqueness theorem.
